cases.answer: Tesla's energy generation and storage gross margin declined in Q2 2026 despite higher revenue due to a larger increase in cost of revenues compared to revenue. Energy generation and storage revenue increased by $350 million, or 13%, year over year, primarily due to increased Megapack deployments, partially offset by a lower average selling price per unit and a decrease in Powerwall deployments [S4]. However, the cost of energy generation and storage revenue increased by $556 million, or 29%, primarily due to deployment fluctuations, an increase in average cost per MWh driven by sales mix, and unfavorable warranty adjustments [S3]. As a result, gross margin for the energy generation and storage segment decreased from 30.3% in Q2 2025 to 20.4% in Q2 2026 [S3].

For the first six months of 2026, free cash flow was $352 million: $8,634 million of operating cash flow less $8,282 million of purchases of property and equipment excluding finance leases, net of sales [S3]. No. Operating cash flow increased, but free cash flow fell because capital spending increased by more. Free cash flow decreased by $458 million from 2025 to 2026 [S3].
